headline: Gulf oil shock, tariff talks and Ontario's vote shaped the week
summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Trump's warnings about new Iran strikes pushed Brent to a six-month high near US$117, feeding 3.1% Canadian inflation and a widely expected Bank of Canada hike on Wednesday. Albertans rejected separation by about 75% to 25% (unofficial), B.C. elected a Conservative majority, Olivia Chow won a second term in Toronto as several GTA incumbents fell, and Ottawa and Washington revived talks on steel and auto tariffs.

top.headline: Gulf attacks push Brent to a six-month high
top.what: Houthi barrages on Saudi Arabia and Trump's talk of new strikes pushed Brent to US$116.72 Friday, its highest since the spring; it was near US$111 Monday as regional security chiefs met in Tehran and U.S. intelligence warned of Iranian plots against Americans.
top.why: This is the single biggest driver of global energy prices this year.

top.headline: Israel votes at a record; exit polls show deadlock
top.what: Exit polls after a record-turnout vote show neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition at 61 seats.
top.why: The outcome shapes Israel's Iran policy and, through it, oil prices.

top.headline: 3.1% inflation sets up an expected Bank of Canada hike
top.what: Gas-driven inflation of 3.1% has most economists expecting a hike to 2.50% on Wednesday.
top.why: A hike would raise costs for variable-rate mortgages and lines of credit.

top.headline: Albertans vote about 75% to stay in Canada
top.what: About three-quarters of Albertans (CBC projected 76.5%) chose to remain in Canada versus roughly a quarter for starting a path toward a separation vote. Premier Danielle Smith said she will not hold another referendum on the issue while she is premier, but that grievances with Ottawa remain.
top.why: Even a non-binding result shapes national politics, federal-provincial relations and investor confidence in the energy sector.

top.headline: B.C. elects a Conservative majority
top.what: Lorne Doerkson's Conservatives won about 64 of 93 seats in unofficial results, ending nine years of NDP government; David Eby resigned as NDP leader.
top.why: A new B.C. government keen on LNG and scrapping the industrial carbon tax could reshape national energy and trade debates.

top.headline: Chow re-elected; GTA voters oust several mayors
top.what: Olivia Chow won about 54% in Toronto, while incumbents fell in Mississauga, Hamilton, Oakville and Milton.
top.why: New councils will set GTA property taxes, housing and transit priorities for four years.

top.headline: U.S. and Canada revive talks on steel and auto tariffs
top.what: Washington reshuffled its 50% tariff list, and Reuters reports the two sides are working on easing steel and auto tariffs, though a deal before the midterms is uncertain.
top.why: Steel and auto tariffs hit thousands of Ontario manufacturing jobs.

top.headline: Forecasters tilt toward a Democratic House
top.what: About 21 million Americans have already voted, courts fought over voter-ID rules and DHS voter probes, and on Friday the Cook Political Report shifted 19 House races toward Democrats.
top.why: The result decides how freely Trump can act on tariffs, the Iran war and spending for the final two years of his term.
